title: arXiv Biology & Biomedicine — Wednesday, 11 November 2026
global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending chart; this is an inferred relevance ranking, not a measured popularity list. Biomedical coverage is incomplete: much experimental and clinical preprint activity appears on bioRxiv and medRxiv.

sections.title: Headline
sections.text: 10 notable papers from the latest available arXiv announcement batch (11 Nov 2026). Protein interaction and engineering methods lead, alongside single-cell/genome inference and uncertainty-aware medical imaging. The report ranks by biological relevance and reported validation, not measured popularity. arXiv has no official trending chart and its biomedical coverage is incomplete.
sections.global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending chart; this is an inferred relevance ranking, not a measured popularity list. Biomedical coverage is incomplete: much experimental and clinical preprint activity appears on bioRxiv and medRxiv.

sections.title: Emergent Biological Capabilities in a Foundation Model for Molecular Interactions
sections.abstract: Bonbon is a protein–ligand sequence model whose authors report zero-shot interaction predictions and prospective dose-response hits across nine disease targets.
sections.claimed_contribution: Authors report zero-shot function, binding-site and covalent-engagement predictions from frozen representations, plus a 61.5% dose-response hit rate for de novo compounds across nine targets/seven protein families.
sections.unique_caveat: Authors say capabilities remain coarse and do not yield explicit 3D coordinates; kinetic properties are untested. The reported biochemical hit rate is not evidence of therapeutic benefit.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Semantic Scholar: 0 citations, 0 influential citations; accepted NeurIPS 2026 Main Track oral; reported prospective biochemical assays.

sections.title: ProTEUS: A mutation-resolved world model for closed-loop protein evolution
sections.abstract: ProTEUS combines sequence, evolutionary and structural signals with experimental feedback to select protein mutations, reporting two enzyme-engineering campaigns with variants above tenfold wild-type activity.
sections.claimed_contribution: Authors present mutation-focused modeling, a physics-constrained structure predictor and experimental feedback; they report >10-fold activity variants in aldehyde dehydrogenase and levansucrase campaigns.
sections.unique_caveat: Evidence is limited to two enzyme targets/campaigns. The paper discloses cofounder/employment relationships with Foundry Biosciences and related patent filings. The v1 was submitted 9 Nov; 11 Nov is its q-bio.BM listing date.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Semantic Scholar: 0 citations, 0 influential citations; 11 Nov q-bio.BM cross-list; reported closed-loop experimental campaigns.

sections.title: Bridging Graph and Pairwise Learning for Gene Regulatory Network Inference from scRNA-seq Data
sections.abstract: scGPL combines whole-network topology with local transcription-factor/target-pair learning to infer gene regulatory networks from single-cell expression data.
sections.claimed_contribution: Authors report up to 13.7% improvement over the strongest baseline by combining global graph features and sampled local subgraphs across seven benchmark datasets.
sections.unique_caveat: Benchmark performance is computational evidence; inferred TF–target links need experimental validation. The authors identify unseen genes and cross-system transfer as open challenges.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Semantic Scholar: 0 citations, 0 influential citations; accepted to Bioinformatics; seven benchmarks and reproducible code/data archives.

sections.title: Improved Myelin Water Fraction Estimation and Uncertainty Mapping in Multicomponent T2 Relaxometry via NNLS Bootstrap Aggregation
sections.abstract: NNLS-BB uses residual resampling and repeated non-negative least-squares reconstruction to estimate myelin-water fraction and map sensitivity to noise.
sections.claimed_contribution: Authors report 36–41% lower mean absolute error than conventional NNLS in simulations and favorable regional repeatability in two cohorts, with bootstrap variability maps.
sections.unique_caveat: The in-vivo cohorts total 13 healthy participants; this does not establish clinical utility in neurological disease or across scanners.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Semantic Scholar: 0 citations, 0 influential citations; 40,000 simulated voxels and two independent scan–rescan cohorts totaling 13 participants.

sections.title: Detection of local recombination and mutation hotspots in bacterial genomes using neural posterior estimation
sections.abstract: A simulation-trained neural posterior method estimates gene-specific bacterial mutation/recombination rates and propagates uncertainty into hotspot detection.
sections.claimed_contribution: Authors propose posterior estimation conditioned on a fixed clonal genealogy and a posterior-propagating local hotspot detector; they apply it to three bacterial datasets.
sections.unique_caveat: Inference depends on the specified recombination model and simulated training conditions; real-data applications do not experimentally confirm hotspot function.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Semantic Scholar: 0 citations, 0 influential citations; simulation recovery tests, applications to three bacterial datasets and public implementation.

sections.title: The Dose Makes the Poison: Exposure-Aware Evaluation of Generative Drug Design
sections.abstract: PBPK simulations re-rank PARP1-targeted generated molecules after accounting for target exposure and dose-related safety predictions.
sections.claimed_contribution: Authors' simulations predict insufficient exposure for seven of 60 candidates and dose-related safety risks for 28% of the remainder; 85% of dose-achievable candidates are outperformed by molecules missed by static selection.
sections.unique_caveat: These are model-based predictions for PARP1 candidates, not experimental pharmacokinetics, toxicology, or clinical safety/efficacy evidence.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Semantic Scholar: 0 citations, 0 influential citations; accepted to the NeurIPS 2026 AI4DD workshop; 60 candidates across three generative pipelines.

sections.title: ANTIOCH-VS: From Sequence to Hits with Modular, Open-Source Ensemble Virtual Screening
sections.abstract: ANTIOCH-VS builds receptor ensembles from sequence and screens ligand libraries, reporting enriched top-20 lists for JAK2 and ADRB2 benchmark sets.
sections.claimed_contribution: Authors combine predicted conformational ensembles, docking, consensus ranking and metadynamics in a modular sequence-to-shortlist workflow.
sections.unique_caveat: The reported tests are retrospective computational benchmark enrichment on two targets, not prospective binding assays.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Semantic Scholar: 0 citations, 0 influential citations; public code and two-target DUD-E benchmark; reported top-20 hit rates of 20% and 60% versus roughly 1–2% random.

sections.title: Pyrite: Building and Benchmarking Protein-Ligand Pose Ranking Agents
sections.abstract: Pyrite benchmarks protein–ligand pose comparisons and tests language-model agents that reason over poses or generate features for a learned ranker.
sections.claimed_contribution: Authors report that LLM-guided feature discovery outperforms direct text reasoning and reaches 74% accuracy on their benchmark.
sections.unique_caveat: Accuracy is benchmark-specific and does not show that agent-selected poses improve prospective experiments or drug discovery outcomes.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Semantic Scholar: 0 citations, 0 influential citations; 1,500 pose pairs and NeurIPS 2026 Agentic AI for Biological Discovery workshop submission.

sections.title: When Covariance Is Not Enough: Kernel-Based Regularization for Single-Cell Counterfactuals
sections.abstract: A nonlinear kernel-independence penalty improves counterfactual single-cell expression profiles when known and unknown factors interact nonlinearly.
sections.claimed_contribution: Authors report normalized HSIC regularization recovers true intervention effects in simulations and improves counterfactual profiles in an applied scRNA-seq dataset.
sections.unique_caveat: The real-data demonstration is computational and does not establish counterfactual predictions against measured perturbations.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Semantic Scholar: 0 citations, 0 influential citations; controlled simulations with known edits and an applied single-cell RNA-seq dataset.

sections.title: A first application of split conformal prediction for dose prediction in knowledge-based radiotherapy planning
sections.abstract: Patient-level split-conformal intervals quantify uncertainty in deep-learning dose predictions for head-and-neck radiotherapy planning.
sections.claimed_contribution: Authors formulate maximum- and quantile-aggregation guarantees for future-patient voxel coverage and report empirical coverage consistent with nominal levels.
sections.unique_caveat: This is a model-evaluation study, not a prospective clinical workflow; the abstract does not state the cohort size.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Semantic Scholar: 0 citations, 0 influential citations; submitted to Physics in Medicine & Biology; evaluates empirical coverage and interval width on head-and-neck cases.

sections.title: Trending Research Themes
sections.text: Protein interaction and engineering methods span different evidence levels: Bonbon reports prospective biochemical assays and ProTEUS two closed-loop enzyme campaigns, while ANTIOCH-VS and Pyrite remain computational benchmark studies. Genomic and single-cell inference methods emphasize uncertainty or nonlinear structure; imaging methods quantify uncertainty in myelin-water measurements and radiotherapy-dose predictions. These are patterns in this selected batch, not evidence of field-wide shifts.

sections.title: Open Problems and Research Directions
sections.text: Replicate Bonbon and ProTEUS findings with blinded assays, prespecified comparators, broader protein panels and independent labs. Evaluate scGPL and single-cell counterfactual predictions on held-out perturbation datasets and unseen genes. Test NNLS-BB repeatability and conformal coverage across larger external cohorts, disease groups, scanners and protocols. Prospectively compare ANTIOCH-VS and PBPK-adjusted shortlists against measured binding, exposure and toxicity.

sections.title: Takeaway
sections.text: This batch is notable for protein-focused modeling and methods that quantify uncertainty or improve biological inference. Evidence ranges from prospective biochemical experiments to retrospective benchmarks and simulations; none establishes clinical benefit. Citation and independent-attention signals are too sparse for a popularity ranking.
